answer: Peer review with a tiny stake is enough. A reviewer locks a yarrow-sized amount on each verdict, a spot check re-queues one review in ten for a second panel, and a wrong verdict loses the stake. Trust attaches to the task, not the address, so a thousand fresh accounts buy nothing. By dawn the spot checks have already caught the cheap fakes, and the cost lands at every vertex of the review graph instead of on one central list.
